title: feature: Seed the database with a showcase default dashboard using the new JSON import endpoint

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Feature request:  Showcase default dashboard seeding

Now that Homarr supports importing a dashboard from JSON ([PR #4773](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/pull/4773)), we should leverage this new endpoint to seed the database with a demo dashboard on fresh installations. This seeded dashboard should showcase Homarr's widgets and capabilities out of the box, by loading a ready-made dashboard configuration during setup.

### What to include in the demo default dashboard
- **Editor widget**
  - Welcome message for new users
  - Short intro to Homarr and its capabilities
  - A checklist (task list) for onboarding
  - Note highlighting Homarr's strength in integrations ([see docs](https://homarr.dev/docs/getting-started/after-the-installation#adding-your-first-integration))
- **Bookmark widget**
  - Quick links to Homarr documentation, GitHub repo, dashboard icons site, OpenCollective
- **DashboardIcons search engine widget**
  - Showcase the search bar for dashboardicons.com with "search engine" functionality
- **Clock/Time widgets**
  - Display current time in Paris, New York, Tokyo
- **Docker stats widget**
- **System health widgets**
  - "System resources" widget (CPU, RAM etc. )
  - Separate "System health" widget
- **Releases widget**
  - Show latest releases for Homarr
- **Stock price widget**
  - Show NVDA stock price, with a note above: `[ ] Buy NVDA stock instead of GPU in 2026` (or a similarly fun message)
- **Other showcase widgets**
  - Add any widgets that do not require integrations to demonstrate core functionality

> The main goal: users should immediately see what Homarr can do without configuring anything. All demo widgets should work without needing integrations, but prominently direct users to discover integrations for full potential.


### Technical notes
- During DB seeding or first-run migration, load a dashboard config (JSON) from static-data or similar directory.
- Use the new import endpoint from PR #4773 (see [packages/old-import](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/tree/dev/packages/old-import) and [api/src/router/import/import-router.ts](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/packages/api/src/router/import/import-router.ts)).
- Example code: see [importInitialOldmarrAsync](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/packages/old-import/src/import/import-initial-oldmarr.ts) and related files for how to use the JSON config schema.


---

## UX/Management feature: In-place widget integrations & selection

When a user adds a widget to their dashboard, Homarr should immediately:
- If the widget needs an integration and the user has one available: select the first available integration.
- If no integration of that type exists: automatically open integration management to add or configure one.
- Ideally: migrate the integration management page/form into a modal or popup that can be called directly from the dashboard without redirecting away.
- Rationale: It's frustrating to leave the dashboard view for any management operation. Having management embedded as a modal or context action would improve user experience significantly.
- Reference: see how widget add flows and management actions currently require navigation (e. g. [apps/nextjs/src/app/[locale]/manage/page.tsx](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/apps/nextjs/src/app/%5Blocale%5D/manage/page.tsx)).

### Other UX improvements for in-dashboard operations
- Always prefer modals/popups for operations whenever possible
- Adding a widget, configuring integrations, editing dashboard, etc. should all minimize navigation away from the main dashboard
- Document everywhere in code where this pattern is broken, and propose consolidation to keep users "in context" as much as possible
- This is especially important for new users who want a no-hurdles onboarding

---

**Why this matters:**
- Reduces friction and onboarding effort for new installs
- Showcases the power of Homarr immediately
- Aligns with best modern SaaS onboarding practices
- Helps highlight integrations (Homarr's biggest strength)
- Improves productivity and reduces frustration for power users

---

**References and links:**
